2608.14843.title: Writing Style Similarity Reflects Academic Genealogy
2608.14843.paper_summary: As authorship attribution systems are increasingly deployed to detect ghostwritten and AI-generated papers, their errors can support accusations against legitimate authors. These systems assume each author's style is their own. Researchers, however, study under advisors, and inherit their stylistic quirks. We build a corpus of arXiv authors with $\geq 2$ solo papers from the Mathematics Genealogy Project graph, giving $5{,}803$ total authors and $2{,}501$ ground-truth advisor-student pairings. Using embeddings from a fine-tuned model, advisors sit $39.9\%$ closer in cosine distance to their students than a random same-field author does. Two open encoders reproduce the effect at $12.6\%$ and $14.5\%$. \emph{Academic siblings}, two students of one advisor who may never have met, sit $30.4\%$ closer across $8{,}360$ pairs, even when they studied at different institutions. Pairs who share only an institution and a field show negligible similarity. Given a closed-set attribution task over the same corpus, the system's errors occur on the true author's advisors and academic siblings $11$ times more often than chance.
2608.14843.paper_summary_zh: 隨著作者歸屬系統越來越多地被用來檢測代寫和 AI 生成的論文，它們的錯誤可能會支持對合法作者的指控。這些系統假設每位作者的風格都是他們自己的。然而，研究者在導師的指導下學習，並繼承了他們的風格特徵。我們建立了一個來自數學家譜系項目圖的 arXiv 作者語料庫，其中包含 $\geq 2$ 篇獨立論文，總共有 $5{,}803$ 位作者和 $2{,}501$ 對真實的導師-學生配對。使用來自微調模型的嵌入，導師與其學生之間的餘弦距離比隨機同領域作者更近 $39.9\%$。兩個開放編碼器分別以 $12.6\%$ 和 $14.5\%$ 重現了這一效果。 \emph{學術兄弟姐妹}，即一位導師的兩位學生，可能從未見過面，在 $8{,}360$ 對中距離更近 $30.4\%$，即使他們在不同的機構學習。僅共享機構和領域的配對顯示出微不足道的相似性。考慮到同一語料庫上的封閉集歸屬任務，系統的錯誤發生在真實作者的導師和學術兄弟姐妹身上，頻率比隨機情況高出 $11$ 倍。
2608.14843.author: Cameron Manzo et.al.
